failure_summary.description: The agent followed a surname-only response or nearby retrieved text instead of answering the clue itself.
Existing guidance to return only a missing component or omit honorifics can conflict with the canonical answer expected.
The answer used the right word family but not the grammatical form requested by the clue.
A bare pair of people was answered with a generic relationship instead of their salient shared affiliation.

patch.reasoning: Clarify when to give a full canonical expression rather than a fragment, and preserve the requested grammatical form. Refine personal-name guidance to avoid surname-only answers while retaining titles when the clue or direct identification makes them relevant. Add targeted guidance for noisy quiz snippets and bare entity pairs.

edits.target: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
edits.content: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For definition clues, match the grammatical form requested by the wording, including inflection, rather than defaulting to the dictionary lemma; give the requested category term and match grammatical number and necessary articles. For a lexical blank, give the missing word, but when the clue asks you to identify a fixed multiword expression or named entity, give its full conventional name even if a component appears in the prompt. When identifying a person, use the conventional given-and-family name rather than a surname alone; give only a missing name component when the prompt explicitly asks for that component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.

edits.target: Use the conventional name without unnecessary expansion: expand an unambiguous familiar nickname to the formal given name, but omit unrequested middle initials, generational suffixes, and honorifics. Conversely, retain an essential entity-type word in an answer naming a publication when needed, as in “Forbes magazine.”
edits.content: Use the conventional name without unnecessary expansion: expand an unambiguous familiar nickname to the formal given name, and retain an established title or style when it is part of direct identification or the clue makes it salient (for example, knighthood may make “Sir” relevant). Omit unrequested middle initials, generational suffixes, and other honorifics. Conversely, retain an essential entity-type word in an answer naming a publication when needed, as in “Forbes magazine.”

For clipped trivia or crossword prompts, distinguish the actual clue from category labels, page headings, and adjacent search-result text; solve the clue rather than repeating those labels. For a bare pair or list of people with no explicit relation, use direct context to identify their salient shared place, affiliation, or category instead of defaulting to a generic relationship.
